Yeah, pretty much everywhere. It's actually why I'm here, honestly. I feel like I'm always running hot, you know? Like I just can't shut the motor off, no matter where I am. And lately, that's been getting me in a lot of trouble at the firehouse. 

Which is really frustrating because, like I said, I want to make lieutenant. The guy who has the spot right now, Miller, he's retiring in six months. He's moving down to Florida, somewhere near Naples, I think. He bought this boat—a center console, maybe 24 feet? He's been talking about it non-stop for the last year. My uncle used to fish for them down in the Keys back in the 90s. He had this little bait shop right off the highway. It smelled terrible, just constantly reeked of frozen squid and chum. But he made a killing selling those little souvenir shark tooth necklaces to tourists. I actually found a fossilized megalodon tooth on the beach once when I was visiting him. It was huge, like the size of my hand. I kept it on my desk for years until my dog knocked it off and it shattered. He's a golden retriever mix, total klutz. His tail is like a whip, it clears the coffee table every time someone rings the doorbell. The mailman actually refuses to come up to the porch now because the dog barks so loud...

Honestly, I think it's the distraction part. It's just... everything pulls my attention away. Like, I'll be trying to fill out a report or check the gear, and just a radio chirp, somebody walking past the bay, or even a thought about a call we had yesterday can completely knock me off what I’m doing. And once I'm off track, it takes me forever to get back to it. 

Like yesterday, I was trying to restock the medical bags on Engine 4, and I heard the dispatcher's voice on the scanner. It wasn't even for our house, it was for a brush fire over in the west district. But it made me think about this massive brush fire we fought a couple years ago during that really dry summer. It was out near the state park, and the wind was just whipping. We were out there for like fourteen hours straight. I remember my boots got completely melted on the soles from the hot ash.
